done_looks_like: End-to-end smoke: running config-diff examples/a.json examples/b.json prints a numbered diff matching examples/expected-diff.txt, accepts numeric index selection, writes a.patched.json byte-identical to examples/expected-patched.json, exits 0; original input files unchanged on disk (mtime + sha256 preserved).

Malformed-input diagnostic path: running config-diff against an unreadable or invalid-JSON file prints a clear error naming the offending file path and parse position to stderr, exits non-zero (>=1), and does NOT write a.patched.json.

Grep-able plain output: when stdout is not a TTY, colour codes are stripped and each diff line begins with a stable token (`+ <path>` / `- <path>` / `~ <path>`); exit code 0 on success, 1 on diagnostic failure, distinguishable for shell composition.

MODULE src/config_diff/differ.py (applicability: business-logic). hides_decision: 'How two arbitrary JSON trees are reduced to an ordered, JSONPath-keyed sequence of added/removed/changed entries with deterministic traversal order (decision likely to change: traversal order, equality semantics for floats/None, container vs leaf threshold).'. Entry-point budget: 1 (`diff_trees`). Strategy seam: none (single in-process implementation; two-adapter rule rules out introducing a DifferStrategy port). Broad interface: invariants=inputs are parsed-json values (dict/list/scalar); ordering=entries are returned in stable depth-first JSONPath order; error_modes=raises DifferError (domain) only -- never propagates json/builtin errors. Bounded context: config-diff core; no ACL needed (caller is in-process applier/CLI). Deletion test (optional): removing this module would force the recursive path-walk + add/remove/change classification to regrow in both the applier (which must align kinds with the patch plan) and the CLI renderer (which prints diff lines) -- two distinct non-test callers, C3 holds.

MODULE src/config_diff/applier.py (applicability: business-logic). hides_decision: 'How an ordered subset of DiffEntry items is replayed against an immutable copy of the target tree to produce a patched tree, including conflict handling when a selected entrys left_value no longer matches (decision likely to change: conflict policy -- strict vs last-write-wins).'. Entry-point budget: 1 (`apply_patch`). Strategy seam: none (only one conflict policy in S01: strict raises ApplierConflict; second policy is hypothetical, two-adapter rule fails -- keep direct). Broad interface: invariants=target tree must be the same shape used to compute diff_entries; ordering=patch entries are applied in their input order, not re-sorted; error_modes=raises ApplierConflict (domain) on stale left_value mismatch -- never mutates inputs. Bounded context: config-diff core. Deletion test (optional): removing this module would force the immutable-copy + selective-apply + conflict-check logic to regrow in the CLI (writing patched file) AND in any future audit-log emitter that needs the post-apply tree -- two distinct non-test callers, C3 holds.

MODULE src/config_diff/parser.py (applicability: cross-system-integration). hides_decision: 'How a filesystem path is read and validated into a parsed-json value with diagnostic-friendly error reporting, isolating callers from stdlib json.JSONDecodeError + OSError vocabulary (decision likely to change: error-message format, source-location precision, future support for JSON5/comments).'. Entry-point budget: 1 (`load_config`). Strategy seam: none. Broad interface: invariants=returned value is one of dict/list/scalar (json types); ordering=N/A (single-shot read); error_modes=raises ConfigReadError(path, position, cause=) -- wraps OSError + json.JSONDecodeError, never leaks foreign exception types. Bounded context: config-diff core; ACL at this module boundary -- wraps stdlib io+json so domain code (differ/applier) never imports json/OSError.

MODULE src/config_diff/cli.py (applicability: framework-shaped -- opt-out of C1-C8 per foundation.md section 3 row 'Framework-mandated shape (CLI command)'). Role: typer-shaped entry point that wires parser -> differ -> selective-prompt -> applier -> file-write and translates ApplierConflict / ConfigReadError / DifferError into stderr + non-zero exit; conforms to typer convention rather than deep-module discipline.

steps: Open a terminal and run: config-diff examples/a.json examples/b.json
Observe the printed numbered diff is colour-coded (ANSI) on a TTY
Enter the indices listed in examples/expected-selection.txt at the prompt
Verify a.patched.json is created in CWD and the process exits 0
Diff a.patched.json against examples/expected-patched.json -- must be byte-identical
